d: Becker learns that an elderly patient, Mr. Fowler, has suffered from a heart attack and calls his daughter to tell her the bad news.
Becker yells at a woman for letting her child cry uncontrollably, then rants about her bad parenting skills.
Becker is outraged as he tells the gang at the diner that someone broke into his apartment and stole his computer.
Becker starts off the day in a cranky mood when he finds a stray cat in his office, which apparently crawled through a broken window.
Becker arrives at the office carrying the parking meter that ate his quarter.
Becker's patient, Jimmy, is a penniless scalper who is unable to afford his ulcer treatment.
On Jake's way out to meet his girlfriend, Becker warns him that his zipper is down.
Becker (Ted Danson) performs his doctorly duties at the diner when a woman begins to choke on her food.
John tries to quit smoking and ends up exchanging one urge for another, sex.
Linda gets a Little Sister and learns a lesson about rebellion while John meddles in Reggies love life.
We learn more about Linda's upbringing and gain insight into her world after a series of mishaps which led her to quit her job. (TV-PG)
Reggie chases a high school fantasy, by reuniting with a high school crush who ends up being a jerk.
Becker has an extra ticket to Chicago and Reggie decides to go.
A friend of and an old friend of Beckers is in town.
Dr. John Becker gets shot and Frances Fisher guest stars as his doctor. (TV-PG)
Frances Fisher guest stars again as Dr. Elizabeth Carson and reveals to Becker her attraction to him
Becker and Liz realize that they have a wacky relationship because they both snoop through each other's stuff and Bob wins and loses to lottery tickets.
We find out how Jake becomes blind and watch him begin to come to terms with the accident, his friend, and himself. (TV-PG)
Becker starts to appreciate life after spending an evening in the morgue identifying one of his patients.
Becker deals with chaos at work while Reggie studies for a test and Margaret attends the reading of a will. (TV-PG)
Becker starts a secretive new health regime to lower his cholesterol, which leads people to talk about his unknown condition. (TV-PG)
Becker is arrested for being confrontational and forced to do community service and Bob moves in with Linda. (TV-PG)
Becker feels old after having to renew his driver's license.
Becker takes a stab at being social by having a dinner party.
Becker fights over a phone bill, Reggie is angry over not being invited to a wedding and Bob gains too much confidence listening to self-help tapes. (TV-PG)
Becker mistakenly tells the wrong family that their father has died, while Margaret and Linda deal with Linda's depressed friend Lynda. (TV-PG)
Becker and Linda have jury duty and Jake gets a seeing-eye-dog. (TV-PG)
Jake goes on a date with a blind girl and Margaret is confronted by the fact that one of her patients doesn't like her. (TV-PG)
Becker gets into a passionate discussion about faith in the power of God versus medicine with a Priest and Jake, Reggie and Bob take a stab at the stock market.
Reggie has a panic attack about where her life is going and Becker confesses that he misses Elizabeth. (TV-PG)
Becker assesses his feelings for Liz when she is offered a new job in Chicago and Linda breaks-up with Gil for lying to her. (TV-PG)
John's four attempts to watch the same movie are annoyingly interrupted, Reggie goes back to school and Hattie discovers her husband's infidelity. (TV-PG)
John is in an awkward situation when his building super is found dead of natural causes
Becker had an ethical decision to make with one of his patients and Reggie is proposed to on her second date with a man. (TV-PG)
Becker is a mentor to a student and Reggie, Bob and Jake come to a standstill in their friendship. (TV-PG)
John is accused of being a creature of habit and as a result, tries a new restaurant.
Becker runs into an old flame and fights with his conscience to spend the night with her because she's a married woman. (TV-PG)
